newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central banker says stocks rise too much.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central banker says stocks rise too much.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong vowed to "closely watch" the island's stock market, saying the share prices have risen "slightly too much" recently.

"The central bank wants to see a stable growth in the stock market. But the share prices have risen slightly too much recently," Sheu told reporters at the Taipei international airport late on Monday.
"The central bank will continue to closely watch (the market movements)," Sheu said after returning from the ASEAN central bankers meeting in Bangkok.
Taiwan share prices closed sharply higher on Monday, exceeding the six-year peak set on Saturday as investors continued to show extreme confidence in the market's upside potential.

On Monday, the weighted index, rising throughout most of the session, ended 88.25 points or 1.16 percent higher at 7,687.28. That surpassed the 7,598.93 point close on Saturday and was the market's highest close since June 2, 1990. Turnover was a T$130.56 billion.
Sheu said, however, the central bank had no intention to curb the stock market by tightening its monetary policy.
"The overheated market is not the result of the central bank's loose monetary policy, the central bank will not try to use its monetary policy to influence the stock market."
In the foreign exchange market, Sheu reiterated the bank's policy to let market forces determine the Taiwan dollar rate.
Dealers have said the bank's recent comments that the Taiwan dollar should follow the U.S. dollar's movements overseas signalled further falls for the local currency.
On Monday, the Taiwan dollar closed at T$27.585 against one U.S. dollar, compared with Saturday's T$27.570 finish.
